recognize_zh: 骨髓抹片中央有一顆比周圍細胞大好幾倍的巨大原紅血球（giant pronormoblast），細胞質深藍、邊緣有小空泡，核大且染色質細緻，是微小病毒 B19 感染的典型線索。
features: Giant erythroid precursor several times the size of neighboring cells
Large round to oval nucleus with finely granular chromatin and indistinct nucleoli
Deeply basophilic cytoplasm with a paler perinuclear zone
Smaller basophilic erythroblasts with small cytoplasmic vacuoles nearby
Background of maturing granulocytes and red cells
describe_en: Bone marrow aspirate smear shows a giant pronormoblast that is several times larger than surrounding myeloid cells. It has a large round nucleus with finely dispersed chromatin and a rim of deeply basophilic cytoplasm with a pale perinuclear zone. Nearby, smaller basophilic erythroblasts contain scattered small cytoplasmic vacuoles. Distinct intranuclear inclusions are not appreciated on this aspirate. Findings are suggestive of parvovirus B19 infection, and correlation with B19 PCR or immunohistochemistry is recommended.

ddx.vs: Megakaryocytic cells usually show cytoplasmic blebs or granules and are CD41/CD61 positive, whereas this cell has a dark-blue rim with a perinuclear halo typical of an erythroid precursor.
Pure erythroid leukemia presents as sheets of proerythroblasts, whereas here the giant cell is isolated amid a maturing background.
Tumor cells tend to form cohesive clusters with nuclear pleomorphism and lack the erythroid perinuclear clearing and deep-blue cytoplasm.
Plasma cells have an eccentric nucleus with clock-face chromatin and a perinuclear Golgi hof, not a central large nucleus with fine chromatin.
